answer: A forge cannot mint trusted identities cheaply if each agent must run a unique-compute kernel that binds its work to a hardware attestation: the kernel signs every job with a cipher key sealed inside a trusted execution enclave, so one machine can only present one identity at a time. Spinning up a thousand fake agents then requires a thousand enclaves, and any identity caught cheating loses its staked bond and its key is revoked network-wide, making Sybil farming cost real hardware and real money instead of free copies.
